newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's negotiator arrives at site for rebel talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru's negotiator arrives at site for rebel talks.

text.p: Peruvian government negotiator Domingo Palermo arrived at the Japanese embassy residence in Lima on Tuesday for peace talks with a spokesman for Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages there, witnesses said.
Palermo appeared in the police security zone around the residence at about 2:55 p.m (1955 GMT).

The long-awaited meeting was set to take place in a two- floor terracotta-coloured building across the street from the diplomatic mansion. The Red Cross, overseeing the talks, erected a big Red Cross flag on the roof.
Palermo was due to meet the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) second-in-command, Rolly Rojas, according to the government.

Before Palermo appeared at the site, Red Cross official Michel Minnig and Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent -- members of a guarantors commission for the talks -- arrived at the site along with Terusuke Tarada, the Japanese government's observer.
The Vatican's representative on the commission, Peruvian Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani, arrived minutes after Palermo.
